question.problem:
Find the equation of the osculating plane (in parametric form) for a curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,1,0)$ where $t=1$, given that

$$
T(1)=\frac{1}{5}(3\,i+4\,k),\,N(1)=j.
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of the point $P(0,1,0)$ is $r(1)=j.$

The osculating plane passes through the point that is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$ The vectors $T(1)$ and $N(1)$ are parallel to this plane. Therefore, the equation of the plane (in parametric form) can be written as

$$
R(s,u)=r(1)+s\,T(1)+u\,N(1),\,s,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

 

Hence, the equation of the osculating plane at the point $(0,1,0)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s,u) & =r(1)+s\,T(1)+u\,N(1) \\  & =j+\frac{s}{5}(3\,i+4\,k)+u(j) \\  & =\frac{3s}{5}\,i+(1+u)\,j+\frac{4s}{5}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
